claims.explanation: Amisulpride is a dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist, and its selective anticancer effects likely reflect dependence of certain tumor cells on dopamine receptor signaling or on the neuroendocrine/autocrine loops it modulates. The pattern of sensitivity is not explained by a single lineage or common driver, but sensitive lines frequently carry TP53 pathway alterations and/or PI3K–AKT–mTOR pathway mutations (PIK3CA, PTEN, STK11), suggesting that loss of these growth-suppressive or metabolic checkpoints increases reliance on DRD2-linked survival signaling. features.basis: amisulpride is a high-affinity DRD2 antagonist; tumors expressing DRD2 are expected to depend on its signaling
most selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations, suggesting loss of p53-mediated survival checkpoints increases dependence on DRD2-linked pathways
PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, implicating PI3K pathway activation in DRD2-dependent survival
PTEN loss co-occurs in several sensitive lines and may amplify PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of DRD2
STK11 mutations appear in sensitive lines, consistent with metabolic/AMPK dysregulation increasing drug sensitivity
ARID1A mutations are more frequent in least-affected lines, suggesting chromatin remodeling loss reduces dependence on DRD2 signaling
KMT2D mutations are enriched in resistant lines, possibly reflecting alternative epigenetic survival programs
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines are among the least affected, indicating strong MAPK-driven survival bypasses DRD2 dependence
ALK-altered neuroblastoma and melanoma lines are resistant, consistent with oncogene addiction overriding DRD2 antagonism
NF2-mutant lines appear in the resistant group, suggesting Hippo pathway activation supports DRD2-independent survival
EGFR-mutant lung lines are among the least affected, indicating EGFR-driven survival compensates for DRD2 blockade
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched in the resistant group, suggesting MAPK pathway activation reduces sensitivity to DRD2 antagonism

raw.explanation: Amisulpride is a dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist, and its selective anticancer effects likely reflect dependence of certain tumor cells on dopamine receptor signaling or on the neuroendocrine/autocrine loops it modulates. The pattern of sensitivity is not explained by a single lineage or common driver, but sensitive lines frequently carry TP53 pathway alterations and/or PI3K–AKT–mTOR pathway mutations (PIK3CA, PTEN, STK11), suggesting that loss of these growth-suppressive or metabolic checkpoints increases reliance on DRD2-linked survival signaling. Conversely, lines with intact or alternative survival signaling (e.g., BRAF-mutant melanomas, ALK-fusion neuroblastomas, and several ARID1A/KMT2D-mutant lines) are relatively protected, consistent with DRD2 antagonism being insufficient when other strong oncogenic drivers dominate.
